verdict.rationale: Mercury Books documents its own reconciliation: accounts are said to reconcile automatically and continuously in real time, and Mercury itself frames this as a starting point for whoever manages the books. But nothing shows a per-account reconciliation view that surfaces matched, unmatched, or duplicate transactions for an accountant to review. The duplicate detection in the pack covers bill pay, not bank reconciliation, so it is an adjacent feature and earns no credit. Missing for 10: a per-bank-account reconciliation workflow against the ledger, surfacing of matched and unmatched transactions, duplicate-transaction detection within reconciliation, a review/approval interface, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an accountant, I can reconcile each bank account against the ledger with matched, unmatched, and duplicate transactions surfaced for review

citations.quote: Accounts reconcile in real time, always reflecting your company's reality, without manual work.
Reconciliation is continuous and real time, ensuring nothing is ever missed.
think of it as giving whoever manages your books a much better starting point
